items.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011
items.q: But like we recorded an album in Alan’s basement and yeah, he’s good at what he does and he’s got good equipment.

ctx.x: What about — things have changed very quickly now for how you record, how your records get out there, how you promote yourself. Is the Internet and YouTube and iTunes, do you think that’s been mostly a good thing?

I think so. For musicians like myself I think it has been. Because even fifteen years ago, or ten, when we first started recording the Soulive albums it had to be in a big studio, you know, like in New York or whatever, they had to be in this huge studio with a big console and everything. We don’t do anything like that now. We don’t need it. But like we recorded an album in Alan’s basement and yeah, he’s good at what he does and he’s got good equipment. He uses ProTools. But that part of it is definitely — it…
And what about a record label? Do you guys do your own?
